turns.prompt_text: My dishwasher is having trouble getting to the detergent Attached 4 files. - 5038.jpg - 5037.jpg - 5036.jpg - 5035.jpg
turns.response_html:
Based on the photos of your Frigidaire dishwasher, there are three very likely reasons the detergent dispenser isn't opening or emptying properly. The good news is that these are usually easy fixes that don't require calling a repair technician.

Here is a breakdown of what is likely happening and how to fix it:

1. The "Tall Item" Obstruction (Most Likely)

Your detergent dispenser has a sliding door (you can see the tracks in the photos). When the cycle starts, a spring pulls that gray door upward to reveal the soap.

  • The Problem: If you place a tall plate, cutting board, or baking sheet in the lower rack right in front of the dispenser, the door hits the item when it tries to slide up. It gets jammed, and the soap never comes out.
  • The Fix: Check the lower rack directly in front of the dispenser. Make sure there are only short items (like small bowls or mugs) in that specific spot so the door has room to slide up freely.

2. The "Sticky" Slide Track

In your close-up photos (especially the last one), the gray plastic tracks where the door slides look a little gunky.

  • The Problem: Over time, old soap residue and food particles build up in those grooves. This creates friction. The spring that opens the door is relatively weak; if the track is sticky, the spring isn't strong enough to snap the door open.
  • The Fix: Take a wet rag or an old toothbrush with some hot water (and maybe a little vinegar) and scrub the grooves on the side of the detergent cup. Slide the door up and down manually a few times to make sure it moves very smoothly.

3. Wet Cup Syndrome

  • The Problem: If the dispenser cup is wet when you put a detergent pod or powder in it, the soap will start to dissolve immediately and stick to the plastic. Even if the door opens, the soap will be glued to the cup and won't fall out.
  • The Fix: Always wipe the cup bone-dry with a paper towel before adding your soap or pod.

A Note on the "Onion Skins"

I noticed a lot of red onion skins/debris scattered in the bottom of the tub in your photo.

  • Why this matters: If your dishwasher filter is clogged with these scraps, the water spray might not be strong enough to rinse the soap out of the cup, even if the door does open.
  • Quick Tip: Check the bottom filter (usually under the bottom spray arm) and remove any wet debris to ensure you have full water pressure.

Try this next: Run a "test" load with the dispenser door closed but empty (no soap). Listen for the "clunk" of it opening about 15-20 minutes into the cycle to see if the mechanical latch is working.
